description: Auto Scaling groups must span at least two Availability Zones, either by specifying two or more availability zones or by using two or more subnets (via VPC zone identifier) located in different Availability Zones.

decisionPoints.description: Whether the Auto Scaling group declares any zone placement at all (neither a list of Availability Zones nor any subnets)
The number of distinct Availability Zones named directly on the Auto Scaling group's zone list (zero/empty, one, duplicates of one, two or more)
The number of subnets referenced by the Auto Scaling group's VPC zone identifier (empty, one, two or more)
Whether the referenced subnets resolve to two or more different Availability Zones, based on the zone assignment of the subnets defined in the same template
Whether the zone list, the subnet list, or the zone assignment of a referenced subnet is only known at deployment time and therefore cannot be resolved during analysis

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group specifies neither a list of Availability Zones nor any subnets for instance placement
requirements.rationale: With neither AvailabilityZones nor VPCZoneIdentifier present, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling applies no default set of zones or subnets, so the group has no documented placement across two or more Availability Zones and cannot satisfy the multi-AZ requirement.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation resource reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup and the EC2 Auto Scaling CreateAutoScalingGroup API reference for the AvailabilityZones / AvailabilityZoneIds / VPCZoneIdentifier properties and any defaults. Both references list AvailabilityZones, AvailabilityZoneIds and VPCZoneIdentifier as "Required: No" but document no default value for any of them — unlike properties such as Cooldown ("Default: 300 seconds") or HealthCheckGracePeriod ("Default: 0 seconds"), the zone/subnet properties carry no default clause at all. AvailabilityZones is described as "A list of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property", and VPCZoneIdentifier as "A list of subnet IDs for a virtual private cloud (VPC) where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created ... Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC." Nothing in the documentation states that omitting both causes the service to populate every Availability Zone in the Region or otherwise place instances in two or more zones; there is no service-applied multi-AZ default. Therefore the resulting group's placement footprint is, per the documentation, not established as spanning two or more Availability Zones, and the rule's condition (two or more AZs, or subnets in two or more distinct AZs) is unmet. No deployment-time-resolved input is involved here — the values are simply absent — so the intrinsic-exception carve-out does not apply. Verdict: flag, decided by the documented absence of any default zone/subnet configuration.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group names exactly one Availability Zone and references no subnets
requirements.rationale: A group whose only zone configuration is a single Availability Zone, with no subnets, launches all instances in that one zone, so the group spans one AZ and fails the two-AZ minimum.
requirements.evidence: Searched AWS docs for the CloudFormation AutoScalingGroup zone properties and for EC2 Auto Scaling multi-AZ guidance. The AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup reference states AvailabilityZones is "A list of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property" — so with exactly one AZ listed and no VPCZoneIdentifier, the group's entire launch footprint is that single zone; the service applies no default that adds further zones, and neither AvailabilityZones nor VPCZoneIdentifier is defaulted to a broader set. The Resilience in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling page (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) directs users to "Span your Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones" and "Maintain at least one instance in each Availability Zone," confirming the rule's intent and that a single-AZ group does not achieve it. The deciding value is explicitly present (one AZ) and known at analysis time, so no deployment-time-unknown exception applies. The resulting runtime state is a single-AZ Auto Scaling group, which breaches the rule.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group names two different Availability Zones and references no subnets
requirements.rationale: The group explicitly enumerates two distinct Availability Zones in AvailabilityZones, so Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling enables and balances capacity across both zones — the multi-AZ span the rule requires — and no subnet list is needed for the group to be zone-redundant.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether naming two Availability Zones (with no VPCZoneIdentifier) is by itself sufficient to make the group span two zones. Searched CloudFormation/CDK reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup AvailabilityZones and VPCZoneIdentifier: VPCZoneIdentifier is documented as "a list of subnet IDs ... Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC" and, when combined with AvailabilityZones, "the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones" — i.e. the two properties are alternative/complementary ways of declaring the group's zones, and AvailabilityZones is not merely decorative. Searched the EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide on multi-AZ behavior: "Auto Scaling automatically balances EC2 instances across zones when you configure multiple zones in your Auto Scaling group settings" (Auto Scaling group Availability Zone distribution / FAQs), and "We strongly recommend that you span your Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones ... you can design applications that automatically fail over between zones for greater resiliency." So with two distinct zones enabled, the service actually operates the group across both, which is exactly the condition the rule tests. No absent-value default is in play here — the deciding value is explicitly present — and the missing subnet list does not reduce the zone count. Therefore the rule owes this configuration no finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a zone list that is present but contains no entries, and references no subnets
requirements.rationale: An empty Availability Zones list with no VPC zone identifier gives the group zero zones — Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling applies no default set of Availability Zones or subnets, so the resulting group cannot span the two zones the rule requires.
requirements.evidence: Searched the CloudFormation resource reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup and the EC2 Auto Scaling CreateAutoScalingGroup API reference for how AvailabilityZones and VPCZoneIdentifier behave when not supplied. Both document AvailabilityZones as "A list of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property" — Required: No, Type: Array of String — and VPCZoneIdentifier as an optional list of subnet IDs, "Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC." Neither the CloudFormation reference nor the API reference documents any service-supplied default value for these properties: there is no statement that Auto Scaling substitutes all zones in the Region or any subnet set when the list is empty. The zone membership of the group is therefore exactly what is enumerated, and an explicitly present but empty list enumerates nothing while no subnets are referenced either. Zero zones is below the rule's minimum of two, and no deployment-time input is involved (the list is present and known to be empty), so the configuration is fully determined at analysis time and breaches the rule.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's zone list contains two entries that are both the same Availability Zone, and references no subnets
requirements.rationale: Two identical entries in the zone list enable only one distinct Availability Zone, so the group has no second zone to fail over to and does not span two Availability Zones as the rule requires.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether duplicate entries in AvailabilityZones can produce a multi-AZ group. I searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup (AvailabilityZones/VPCZoneIdentifier) and the EC2 Auto Scaling user guide for multi-AZ distribution and resilience. The AvailabilityZones property is simply the list of zones enabled for the group; EC2 Auto Scaling operates on the set of *enabled* Availability Zones — it "automatically tries to maintain equivalent numbers of instances in each enabled Availability Zone" and, when a zone fails, "launches new instances in different Availability Zones enabled for your Auto Scaling group" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-benefits.html). Listing the same zone name twice enables exactly one distinct zone; there is no second enabled zone into which instances could be launched, so the resource deployed is functionally single-AZ. No subnets are referenced, so VPCZoneIdentifier provides no additional zones. The resilience guidance explicitly directs users to "Span your Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones," which this configuration does not do. No default value is at issue here — the zone list is explicitly present and resolves to one zone — and nothing is deferred to deployment time, so the intrinsic-value exception does not apply.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references exactly one subnet, defined in the same template, and names no Availability Zones
requirements.rationale: A single subnet resides entirely within one Availability Zone and cannot span zones, so an Auto Scaling group whose only zone source is one subnet — with no AvailabilityZones listed — runs in exactly one Availability Zone.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on how many Availability Zones one subnet can supply to an Auto Scaling group. Searched CloudFormation/reference docs for VPCZoneIdentifier semantics: the AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup VPCZoneIdentifier property is "a list of subnet IDs for a virtual private cloud (VPC) where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created," and when combined with AvailabilityZones the subnets must reside in those zones — i.e. the subnets are what determine the zones the group covers (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/quickref-ec2-auto-scaling.md, which illustrates multi-AZ coverage by listing three subnets in three different Availability Zones). Searched VPC docs for subnet-to-AZ cardinality: "Each subnet must reside entirely within one Availability Zone and cannot span zones" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/configure-subnets.html). Here the group names no AvailabilityZones, so its zone coverage comes solely from the one referenced subnet, which is confined to a single zone; there is no default that adds further zones — omitting AvailabilityZones does not expand coverage beyond the supplied subnets. The subnet being declared in the same template does not change this: whatever Availability Zone that subnet resolves to at deployment time (even if the AZ itself is a parameter or Fn::Select), the count is one, so every possible resolution breaches the rule and the deployment-time-unknown exception does not apply. The resource therefore ends up spanning fewer than two Availability Zones and the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group has a subnet reference list that is present but contains no entries, and names no Availability Zones
requirements.rationale: An empty subnet list supplies zero subnets and, with no Availability Zones named either, the group has no way to reach the two-AZ minimum — there is no service default that fills in additional subnets or zones.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether an empty VPCZoneIdentifier list plus absent AvailabilityZones could still yield a group spanning two or more AZs by service default. Searched the EC2 Auto Scaling API reference (CreateAutoScalingGroup) and the CloudFormation resource reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup. CreateAutoScalingGroup documents both AvailabilityZones and VPCZoneIdentifier as arrays that the caller supplies; AvailabilityZones is described as "A list of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property" — i.e. the zones used come from whichever list is given, and no default zone set is documented that would expand an empty list. The CloudFormation reference marks VPCZoneIdentifier as Conditional ("Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC") and, where both are given, the subnets must reside in the specified zones; nothing in either page states that an empty array is backfilled with all zones in the Region or with a default subnet per zone. So the deployed group's zone coverage is whatever the (empty) list provides: zero subnets and zero named zones, which cannot satisfy a two-AZ minimum. The list is present but empty, so this is not an analysis-time unknown — the value is fully known and known to be insufficient. Flag, settled by the documented semantics of these two properties.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references two subnets defined in the same template, each assigned to a different Availability Zone, and names no Availability Zones
requirements.rationale: The group's VPCZoneIdentifier lists two subnets whose in-template AvailabilityZone properties are different, so the deployed Auto Scaling group launches instances across two Availability Zones even though no AvailabilityZones are named on the group itself.
requirements.evidence: Searched CloudFormation and CDK reference docs for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup VPCZoneIdentifier vs AvailabilityZones. The AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup reference states AvailabilityZones is "A list of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property" — i.e. AvailabilityZones is not required, and is the alternative to VPCZoneIdentifier, not a supplement to it. VPCZoneIdentifier is documented as "A list of subnet IDs for a virtual private cloud (VPC) where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created... Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC. If you specify VPCZoneIdentifier with AvailabilityZones, the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones." The CloudFormation quick-reference example for EC2 Auto Scaling shows exactly this pattern: a group with VPCZoneIdentifier listing subnets "in three different Availability Zones" and no AvailabilityZones property. So the AZ span of a group configured this way is determined by the subnets' zones. Here both referenced subnets are declared in the same template with distinct AvailabilityZone values, so the zone span is fully resolvable at analysis time — two distinct AZs — with no deployment-time unknown. The rule's own wording admits this route ("or by using two or more subnets (via VPC zone identifier) located in different Availability Zones"), and the resulting service state satisfies it. Nothing about the omitted AvailabilityZones property degrades the deployed configuration, so there is no finding to report.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references two subnets defined in the same template that are both assigned to the same Availability Zone, and names no Availability Zones
requirements.rationale: Both subnets referenced by VPCZoneIdentifier are declared in the same template with the same AvailabilityZone, so the group can only launch instances into that single zone — no AvailabilityZones default fills the gap, since EC2 Auto Scaling derives the group's zones from the subnets given.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on how many distinct Availability Zones the deployed Auto Scaling group will actually span when only VPCZoneIdentifier is given. Searched the AWS docs for "Auto Scaling group VPCZoneIdentifier subnets availability zones" and the CloudFormation AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup reference. The VPCZoneIdentifier documentation (CFN reference, mirrored in the CDK CfnAutoScalingGroupProps docs) describes it as "a list of subnet IDs for a virtual private cloud (VPC) where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created" and states that if VPCZoneIdentifier is specified together with AvailabilityZones, "the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones" — i.e. the subnets are the authoritative source of the group's zonal footprint, and Auto Scaling launches only into the AZs of the supplied subnets. There is no default that adds extra Availability Zones when AvailabilityZones is omitted; omitting it simply means the zone set equals the zones of the listed subnets. The CloudFormation Auto Scaling quick-reference reinforces this by describing multi-AZ coverage as "a list of existing subnets in three different Availability Zones", i.e. AZ spread is achieved through the subnet list. Here both referenced subnets are AWS::EC2::Subnet resources in the same template with the same AvailabilityZone value, so the resolved zone set has exactly one member. This is not an analysis-time unknown — the subnets' AZs are readable from the template — so the intrinsic-exception does not apply. The resource will run in a single Availability Zone, breaching the rule's two-AZ minimum, so the rule owes a finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references three subnets defined in the same template, two of which share one Availability Zone while the third is in another Availability Zone
requirements.rationale: The group's VPC zone identifier lists three in-template subnets whose Availability Zone properties resolve to two distinct zones, so the group's instances will be distributed across two Availability Zones, which meets the rule's minimum regardless of two subnets duplicating one zone.
requirements.evidence: What the verdict turns on: whether a subnet list containing duplicate Availability Zones still yields coverage of two or more distinct zones. Searched AWS docs for "Auto Scaling group VPCZoneIdentifier multiple subnets Availability Zones" and "Auto Scaling group multiple Availability Zones high availability recommendation". The EC2 Auto Scaling user guide ("Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture", Example: Distribute instances across Availability Zones) states that when you create an Auto Scaling group you choose the VPC and subnets where it deploys, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling creates instances in the chosen subnets, and "Each subnet must reside entirely within one Availability Zone and cannot span zones" — so each referenced subnet contributes exactly one zone, and the set of zones covered by the group is the set of distinct zones of its subnets. It also notes you can define one or more subnets in each Availability Zone, confirming multiple subnets legitimately map to the same zone without reducing zone coverage. The CloudFormation/CDK reference for VPCZoneIdentifier confirms this property is the list of subnets in which instances can be created. Here the subnets are defined in the same template, so their AvailabilityZone values are statically resolvable at analysis time: two subnets in one zone plus one subnet in another gives two distinct zones. The redundant subnet in the first zone is additive capacity, not a deficiency; the group's running configuration spans two Availability Zones, satisfying the rule. No documented default is involved because VPCZoneIdentifier is explicitly supplied.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references two subnets defined in the same template whose placement is expressed as zone identifiers rather than zone names, and the two identifiers differ
requirements.rationale: Each subnet sits in exactly one Availability Zone and an AZ ID is a unique identifier for a single Availability Zone, so two subnets carrying two different zone identifiers are in two different Availability Zones and the group's VPC zone identifier already spans the required two zones.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether expressing a subnet's placement as an Availability Zone ID (AvailabilityZoneId, e.g. use1-az1) rather than an Availability Zone name (AvailabilityZone, e.g. us-east-1a) still lets the scanner conclude that two in-template subnets referenced by the ASG's VPCZoneIdentifier are in distinct Availability Zones.

Searched CloudFormation/reference docs for "AWS::EC2::Subnet AvailabilityZoneId property": AWS::EC2::Subnet accepts both AvailabilityZone and AvailabilityZoneId, and AvailabilityZoneId is documented as "The AZ ID of the subnet" — i.e. an alternative, equally definitive expression of the single Availability Zone the subnet occupies (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-subnet.html#cfn-ec2-subnet-availabilityzoneid).

Searched general docs for AZ ID semantics: "Availability Zone IDs for your AWS resources" (AWS RAM User Guide) states "An AZ ID is a unique and consistent identifier for an Availability Zone across all AWS accounts. For example, use1-az1 is an AZ ID for an Availability Zone in the us-east-1 Region and it represents the same physical location in every AWS account." The Global Infrastructure "AZ IDs" page says the same. So AZ IDs map one-to-one to Availability Zones; two distinct AZ IDs necessarily denote two distinct Availability Zones (whereas two distinct AZ names could in principle be aliases only across accounts, never within one). Nothing here is deployment-time-unknown: both identifiers are literal, differing values present in the template.

Applying the rule: the ASG satisfies the two-AZ requirement "by using two or more subnets (via VPC zone identifier) located in different Availability Zones." The two referenced subnets are provably in different Availability Zones, so the resource as deployed spans two AZs. The rule's intent — multi-AZ resilience — is met; flagging here would be a false positive caused solely by the template using AZ IDs instead of AZ names as the placement expression. No default value is at stake since placement is explicitly given for both subnets.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references two subnets by literal subnet identifiers of subnets not defined anywhere in the template, so their Availability Zone assignments are not available during analysis
requirements.rationale: The group supplies two distinct pre-existing subnet IDs, and since each subnet's Availability Zone is account state outside the template, whether they span two zones cannot be determined at analysis time, so no breach can be asserted.
requirements.evidence: What the verdict turns on: whether two literal subnet IDs in VPCZoneIdentifier can be shown to sit in two different Availability Zones. Searched AWS docs for "Auto Scaling group VPCZoneIdentifier subnets Availability Zones" and "subnet resides in a single Availability Zone VPC". The VPC User Guide (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/configure-subnets.html) states "Each subnet must reside entirely within one Availability Zone and cannot span zones" — so each referenced subnet maps to exactly one AZ, but the mapping itself is a property of the existing subnet in the account, not of the template. The Auto Scaling CloudFormation reference for VPCZoneIdentifier (quickref-ec2-auto-scaling and CfnAutoScalingGroup docs) confirms the property takes "a list of existing subnet IDs ... You must specify the applicable subnet IDs from your account before you create your stack," and only constrains AZs when AvailabilityZones is also given ("the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones"). No documentation supplies a default AZ, an implied AZ-per-subnet-ID rule, or any guarantee that two arbitrary subnet IDs are same-AZ or cross-AZ. Because the subnets are not declared in the template, the deciding fact (each subnet's AZ) is unresolvable during static analysis, and both outcomes remain possible — two subnets in different AZs (compliant) or two subnets in the same AZ (non-compliant). Since not every possible resolution breaches the rule, the scanner cannot assert a violation, and the analysis-time-unknown exception applies: the rule should not fire.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's list of Availability Zones comes entirely from an input value supplied at deployment time, and no subnets are referenced
requirements.rationale: The number and identity of Availability Zones is supplied by a deployment-time input, so the scanner cannot know at analysis time whether the group ends up in one zone or several, and a parameter can legitimately supply two or more AZs — the breach is not established.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on how many distinct Availability Zones the Auto Scaling group will actually span. Here the entire AvailabilityZones list comes from a parameter/input resolved at deployment time and there is no VPCZoneIdentifier to inspect, so the deciding value (the list's contents and length) is not visible when the template is scanned. I checked the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup (AvailabilityZones / VPCZoneIdentifier) and the EC2 Auto Scaling resilience guidance (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html), which confirms the rule's intent ("Span your Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones") but establishes no service-applied default that would fill in or expand a caller-supplied AvailabilityZones list: whatever AZs the parameter resolves to are exactly the zones enabled for the group. Because the input can validly resolve to two or more AZs (e.g. a List<AWS::EC2::AvailabilityZone::Name> parameter with several values), it is not the case that every possible value breaches the rule, so the "known outcome regardless of input" carve-out does not apply. This is a genuine analysis-time unknown rather than a merely absent value — the property is present and populated, just from an external input — so the rule owes no finding here.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's list of subnet references comes entirely from an input value supplied at deployment time, and no Availability Zones are named
requirements.rationale: The AZ span is determined entirely by a subnet list supplied at deployment time, so the number of subnets and the Availability Zones they sit in are unknown at analysis time, and that list may legitimately contain two or more subnets in different zones, so no breach can be asserted.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether the scanner can determine how many Availability Zones the group will span. Here the VPCZoneIdentifier (subnet references) resolves from a deployment-time input, and AvailabilityZones is not specified. Searched CloudFormation/EC2 Auto Scaling reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup VPCZoneIdentifier and AvailabilityZones (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup.md): both properties are optional; AvailabilityZones is "a list of Availability Zones where instances ... can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property", and VPCZoneIdentifier is "Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC". Neither documents a service-applied default that guarantees or denies multi-AZ coverage; the zones the group spans are derived from whichever subnets are supplied, and each subnet resides entirely within one AZ (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-benefits.html). Because the supplied list can hold one subnet (single AZ, breaching) or several subnets in distinct AZs (compliant), not every possible input value breaches the rule, so the outcome is genuinely unresolvable until deployment. This is the deployment-time-unknown exception rather than a mere absence of configuration: the property is present, only its value is deferred. Therefore the rule owes no finding here.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group references two subnets defined in the same template whose Availability Zone assignments each come from input values supplied at deployment time
requirements.rationale: The Auto Scaling group's zone spread depends on the Availability Zone each referenced subnet resolves to, and those AZ values come from deployment-time inputs, so the scanner cannot know whether the two subnets land in different zones — and since the inputs can legitimately resolve to two distinct AZs, a breach is not certain.
requirements.evidence: What the verdict turns on: whether the two subnets referenced by the group's VPC zone identifier sit in different Availability Zones. Searched the CloudFormation reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup VPCZoneIdentifier semantics (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/quickref-ec2-auto-scaling.md and the CfnAutoScalingGroupProps reference) — VPCZoneIdentifier is a list of subnet IDs, and the zone coverage of the group is entirely derived from the zones of those subnets ("the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones"). It carries no default that would add a second zone: an ASG built on subnets that all sit in one zone is single-AZ. Then searched the AWS::EC2::Subnet reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-subnet.md): AvailabilityZone is an optional String property, and the Parameters documentation shows the idiomatic pattern of feeding it from a parameter (e.g. !Select from a CommaDelimitedList parameter of AZ names). Nothing in the documentation constrains a parameter-supplied AZ value, so each subnet's zone is unresolvable until the stack is deployed. Because the AZ assignments of both subnets come from deployment-time inputs, the resulting configuration is unknown at analysis time; and the possible resolutions include two distinct AZs (compliant) as well as the same AZ twice (non-compliant), so it is not the case that every possible value breaches the rule. This is the deployment-time-unknown exception rather than a merely absent value, so the rule owes no finding.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group names one Availability Zone and also references a single subnet defined in the same template that is assigned to a different Availability Zone
requirements.rationale: One named Availability Zone plus one subnet is single-zone capacity on either dimension, and because AWS requires subnets given in VPCZoneIdentifier to reside in the Availability Zones listed in AvailabilityZones, the mismatched subnet cannot add a second usable zone — it makes the configuration invalid rather than multi-AZ.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether an ASG that lists exactly one Availability Zone and exactly one subnet — with that subnet placed in a different AZ than the one listed — can be counted as spanning two Availability Zones. Searched CloudFormation and Auto Scaling API references for the interaction of AvailabilityZones and VPCZoneIdentifier. The AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup resource reference (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup.md) states for VPCZoneIdentifier: "Required to launch instances into a nondefault VPC. If you specify VPCZoneIdentifier with AvailabilityZones, the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones." The same constraint appears in the CreateAutoScalingGroup API/SDK docs. The CreateAutoScalingGroup reference also describes AvailabilityZones as being used "for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the VPCZoneIdentifier property" — i.e. when subnets are supplied, the subnets determine where instances launch, so the effective footprint here is one subnet in one AZ. Either way the group is single-zone: the AZ list contributes one zone, the subnet list contributes one zone, and the documented rule forbids treating the cross-AZ pairing as a legitimate two-zone span (the create request violates the stated constraint). No default fills in additional zones or subnets — Auto Scaling does not expand a single-AZ/single-subnet group across zones on its own. Both values are declared in the template (the subnet is defined in the same template with an explicit differing AvailabilityZone), so nothing is unresolvable at analysis time. The rule's requirement of two or more AZs, or two or more subnets in different AZs, is unmet.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group's zone list contains one literal Availability Zone name plus one entry taken from an input value supplied at deployment time, and references no subnets
requirements.rationale: The group declares two availability-zone entries, and the second comes from a deployment-time input whose value determines whether the two entries are distinct zones — since a value naming a different Availability Zone satisfies the multi-AZ requirement, the outcome is not knowable at analysis time and no breach can be asserted.
requirements.evidence:
What the verdict turns on: whether the two entries in the Auto Scaling group's zone list resolve to two different Availability Zones. There are no subnets, so the VPCZoneIdentifier path cannot supply zone spread; the AvailabilityZones list is the only evidence. One entry is a literal AZ name; the other is a deployment-time input (e.g. a CloudFormation parameter or equivalent), so its value is unknown to a scanner.

Searches performed: (1) CloudFormation/reference search for "AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup AvailabilityZones VPCZoneIdentifier", which confirms AvailabilityZones and VPCZoneIdentifier are the two properties that establish zone coverage, that VPCZoneIdentifier subnets must reside in the specified AvailabilityZones, and that multi-AZ coverage is expressed as multiple list entries (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup.md, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cdk/api/v2/docs/aws-cdk-lib.aws_autoscaling.CfnAutoScalingGroupProps.html). (2) General search on multi-AZ Auto Scaling guidance, which confirms the underlying requirement — AWS "strongly recommend[s] that you span your Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones," and each AZ is identified by a distinct name such as us-east-1a (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-benefits.html). Nothing in the documentation says the service deduplicates, expands, or otherwise transforms the list in a way that would decide this case; there is no default zone that a supplied value would fall back to, because the value is explicitly provided by the input.

Why this decides pass: the deployed configuration has exactly two zone entries. If the input resolves to an AZ different from the literal, the group spans two Availability Zones and is compliant. If it happens to resolve to the same AZ as the literal, the group effectively spans one zone and would breach. Both outcomes are reachable, so this is not a case where every possible input value breaches the rule — the deciding value is a genuine analysis-time unknown resolved only at deployment. A scanner cannot assert a breach, so the rule owes no finding here.

requirements.description: Auto Scaling group whose subnet list (VPC zone identifier) consists of exactly one entry — a single subnet reference (or single subnet ID) whose Availability Zone is supplied by a deployment-time input — and no Availability Zones are named. The equivalent single-entry case on the zone side (a zone list holding exactly one entry taken from a deployment-time input) is the same gap.
requirements.rationale: A subnet lives in exactly one Availability Zone, so a VPC zone identifier (or availability zone list) with a single entry yields an Auto Scaling group confined to one AZ no matter which zone the deployment-time input resolves to.
requirements.evidence: The verdict turns on whether a one-element subnet list can ever satisfy "spans at least two Availability Zones" when the subnet's AZ is only known at deploy time. Searched AWS docs for "Auto Scaling group VPCZoneIdentifier subnets multiple Availability Zones" and "Auto Scaling group span multiple Availability Zones best practice resilience". The CloudFormation/CDK reference for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup VPCZoneIdentifier describes it as "a list of subnet IDs for a virtual private cloud (VPC) where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created" and notes that if VPCZoneIdentifier is specified with AvailabilityZones, "the subnets that you specify for this property must reside in those Availability Zones" — i.e. the group's enabled zones are derived from the subnets supplied. "Resilience in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) states the requirement the rule encodes: "Span your Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones" and "Maintain at least one instance in each Availability Zone", with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling using the group's enabled Availability Zones to maintain high availability. Because a VPC subnet is contained in exactly one Availability Zone, a VPC zone identifier holding exactly one subnet enables exactly one zone, and the same holds for an AvailabilityZones list holding exactly one entry. The deployment-time input therefore does not create an analysis-time unknown that matters: every possible value the input could resolve to (any single subnet, any single zone name) produces a single-AZ group, so the outcome is known regardless of which value is chosen and the intrinsic-value exception does not apply. There is no service default that adds a second zone — Auto Scaling only balances across the zones the configuration enables. Flag.

removedRequirements.description: Auto Scaling group names three different Availability Zones and references no subnets
removedRequirements.reason: Same decision-point state as two distinct zones named directly (two or more); no additional branch.

removedRequirements.description: Auto Scaling group names one Availability Zone and also references a single subnet defined in the same template that is assigned to that same Availability Zone
removedRequirements.reason: The rule's purpose is to ensure an Auto Scaling group actually has capacity spread across two or more Availability Zones. REQ-14 only conflicts because its second test asserts that one named zone plus one subnet in a *different* zone is acceptable multi-AZ placement — that drifts from the rule's purpose: a single named AZ plus a single subnet is one-zone capacity on either dimension, and AWS requires VPCZoneIdentifier subnets to lie within the listed AvailabilityZones, so the mismatch cannot create a second usable zone. Keeping REQ-14 would make the rule permissive toward a configuration that is both single-AZ and invalid, a silent miss. REQ-18 preserves the flagging behavior for that same byte-for-byte input, so the rule continues to fail visibly and correctably; a genuinely single-AZ group (one zone, one subnet) is still flagged under REQ-18's single-zone-capacity reasoning, so real coverage loss is minimal. (research had settled it as: The group's instances are confined to a single Availability Zone — the one AZ it names, which is also the AZ of its one referenced subnet — so it spans one zone rather than the two the rule requires.)
